title: Swap Nodes in Pairs
statement:
You are given the head of a singly linked list. Swap every two adjacent nodes and return the head of the modified list: the 1st and 2nd nodes swap, the 3rd and 4th nodes swap, and so on. If the list has an odd number of nodes, the last node stays where it is.

You must rearrange the **nodes themselves** by changing their `next` links. Changing the values stored in the nodes is not allowed (the tests only compare the resulting order of values, but an interviewer will check your pointer work).

**Follow-up:** Solve it in `O(1)` extra space, and then think about how the same idea extends to reversing the list in groups of `k` nodes.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`, the number of nodes.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers: the node values from head to tail.
outputFormat: Print the node values of the resulting list from head to tail, space-separated.

examples.explanation: Nodes 10 and 20 swap, then nodes 30 and 40 swap.
Two pairs swap; the fifth node has no partner, so it stays last.
A single node has nothing to swap with.

hints: A dummy node before the head removes the special case for swapping the first pair.
Keep a pointer `prev` to the node just before the current pair. With `a = prev.next` and `b = a.next`, you must rewire three links: `prev -> b`, `a -> b.next`, `b -> a`.
After a swap, `a` is the tail of the processed part, so move `prev` to `a` and repeat while two nodes remain.

import sys
from typing import Optional


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next


def swap_pairs(head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
    # Write your solution here
    return head


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    dummy = ListNode()
    cur = dummy
    for i in range(n):
        cur.next = ListNode(int(data[1 + i]))
        cur = cur.next
    head = swap_pairs(dummy.next)
    out = []
    while head:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    print(' '.join(map(str, out)))
